name: Leave-one-out labeling baseline (ours vs LOO-trained pruners, LOO vs equal-cost K=11 Ridge)
fixed: 2026-10-02, before any LOO or K=11 label, pruner or arm (ours_loo, loo_sent, ours_k11, k11_sent, loocomp_bin*) was measured, trained or evaluated anywhere
documents: test split, per source the documents ranked 501-2500 in hash order (select --n 2000 --offset 500, the round-2 replication set); vimqa has 199 (501-699)
arms: run_pipeline.sh LOO_ARMS=1: ours_loo / loo_sent = pruner_loo (LOO labels, ours_beta's loss), ours_k11 / k11_sent = pruner_k11 (the method's Ridge on 11 of the existing random masks: about the LOO call count), each with seed reruns _s1/_s2; the LooComp-style binary pruner (LOO_BIN=1: loocomp_bin, loocomp_bin_sent) is exploratory, in no family
seeds: as in the existing families: a supported test is also reported 'every seed agrees' when every seed rerun of the tested arm (<ours>_s<k>) points the same way against the fixed comparison arm
two_sided: the schema tests one-sided claims only; L2 (ours_k11 vs ours_loo, no direction fixed) is split into L2a and L2b, one per direction, each at alpha 0.025 with Holm within it: a two-sided test at 0.05 per family pair. At most one of the two can be supported for a given cell

families.name: L1
families.claim: ours_sent > loo_sent at 8x: random-mask Ridge attribution labels beat leave-one-out labels at sentence level (primary reader)

families.name: L1p
families.claim: ours_beta > ours_loo, paragraph selection at 4x and 8x: the same comparison as L1 without the sentence step (primary reader)

families.name: L2a
families.claim: ours_k11 > ours_loo at 4x and 8x: at equal labeling cost (~11 reader calls per document), random masks + Ridge beat LOO (primary reader; one direction of a two-sided test, alpha 0.025)

families.name: L2b
families.claim: ours_loo > ours_k11 at 4x and 8x: at equal labeling cost, LOO beats random masks + Ridge (primary reader; the other direction of L2a, alpha 0.025)
